newsitem.title: USA: AMCOL unit to raise polymer prices.
newsitem.headline: AMCOL unit to raise polymer prices.

text.p: AMCOL International Corp said Monday its Chemdal Corp subsidiary will raise prices of its superabsorbent polymers by $0.04 a pound, effective December 1.
The polymers, a class of specialty chemicals, are used as absorption agents in baby diapers, adult incontinence products and other personal care items.

"Chemdal's economic advantages have enabled it to produce reasonable margins in the highly competitive (superabsorbent polymer) market," Chemdal President Larry Washow said in a statement. "While Chemdal continues to view its economic position as favorable, the demands of continuing technological and product innovation, coupled with increasing market demand, are driving the market, as a whole, to demand higher returns from the (superabsorbent polymer) business."
While the superabsorbent polymer market has seen over-capacity and declining margins for some time, industry dynamics are changing, added Greg Meyer, Chemdal vice president of marketing.
He said demand appears to be rising and will more closely match supply requirements through 1998, which could have additional impact on pricing.
"Also, there is demand for newer generation products and a need for corresponding investments to meet future technology requirements," Meyer said.
